summary: Noel Showwalter Curtis is charged with felony theft dated Oct. 19 in one of seven criminal cases opened in the Fairbanks area on Oct. 29. Fairbanks police arrested Jared Graydon Wheelock on a domestic violence assault charge early Oct. 29, and troopers reported a theft from a gas station overnight. Troopers arrested a 20-year-old Nenana man after a disturbance near the village on Oct. 28, and Fairbanks police recorded a harassment arrest on Cushman Street the same afternoon. A change-of-plea hearing has been set in the Fairbanks armed robbery case against Daniel Zachary Schwietert, arraignments were held in three other Fairbanks felony cases, and an arraignment was held in the Anderson assault case against Gregory Steven Ashley. The Alaska Court System's weekly report for Oct. 22 to 28 counts 46 new criminal cases at Fairbanks, one at Nenana, one at Delta Junction and none at Healy; those are the report's own counts, and they do not include eleven case numbers the Fairbanks court opened on Oct. 28, which the report omits.

entries.title: Felony theft charge: Noel Showwalter Curtis
body: Noel Showwalter Curtis is charged with second-degree theft, taking property worth $750 to $24,999, a Class C felony punishable by up to five years.
The charge is dated Oct. 19 at Fairbanks. Case 4FA-26-02195CR, filed Oct. 29.

entries.title: DV assault charge: Jared Graydon Wheelock
body: Jared Graydon Wheelock, 54, is charged with fourth-degree assault, recklessly injuring someone, a Class A misdemeanor recorded as domestic violence.
Fairbanks Police record the arrest at the 1600 block of Southern Avenue at 12:11 a.m. on Oct. 29. Police case 26003307.
Case 4FA-26-02193CR; arraigned Oct. 29, pre-trial conference Dec. 24.

entries.title: DUI arrest: Rion Scoville Smith
body: Rion Scoville Smith was arrested on a charge of driving under the influence, troopers say.

Troopers say they stopped his car at about 10:58 p.m. on Oct. 23 after an improper left turn that nearly caused a collision, and that he gave a breath sample of .086. Alaska State Troopers case AK26105625.

entries.title: Theft from a Fairbanks gas station
body: Troopers are investigating a theft from a gas station reported at about 1:16 a.m. on Oct. 29. No one has been named. Alaska State Troopers case AK26106995.

entries.title: DV unlawful contact charge: Pavel Ivanovich Budnik
body: Pavel Ivanovich Budnik is charged with unlawful contact in breach of a court order, contacting someone a court order forbids contacting, a Class A misdemeanor recorded as domestic violence.
The charge is dated Oct. 10 at Fairbanks. Case 4FA-26-02196CR; arraignment Oct. 30.

entries.title: Criminal mischief and harassment arrest: Thomas Olson
body: Thomas Olson, 20, of Nenana, was arrested on charges of criminal mischief in the fifth degree, which troopers record as domestic violence, harassment in the second degree, and resisting arrest. Near Nenana, Oct. 28 at 6:35 p.m.; Alaska State Troopers.

Troopers say they received a report of a disturbance near Nenana and that their investigation led to the arrest, and that Olson resisted arrest with force, for which the resisting charge was added. He was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center and held without bail pending arraignment.

Alaska State Troopers case AK26106959. The court case, 4NE-26-00105CR, charges fifth-degree criminal mischief, damage under $250, a Class B misdemeanor recorded as domestic violence. He was arraigned Oct. 29; rural calendar call Dec. 15 at Nenana.

entries.title: Harassment arrest: Nicole Renae Muzzana
body: Nicole Renae Muzzana, 45, was arrested on a charge of harassment in the first degree — offensive contact with blood or another bodily fluid — recorded by police as a misdemeanor. 600 block of Cushman Street, Fairbanks, Oct. 28 at 4:39 p.m.; Fairbanks Police.
Police case 26003304. The court case, 4FA-26-02192CR, charges first-degree harassment as a Class A misdemeanor. Arraignment Nov. 3.

entries.title: Change of plea set in armed robbery case: Daniel Zachary Schwietert
body: Daniel Zachary Schwietert, 25, of Fairbanks, is charged with robbery in the first degree — taking property by force while armed with a deadly weapon — a Class A felony, punishable by up to 20 years.
Troopers say they were called to Beaver Sports in Fairbanks at 1:46 p.m. on Oct. 12 for a reported robbery and arrested him.

A bail hearing was held on Oct. 28 and a change-of-plea hearing is set for Oct. 30. A pre-trial conference is set for Nov. 5 and a trial week for Nov. 16. Case 4FA-26-02078CR. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Arraignments held in three Fairbanks felony cases
body: Jordan Henry Williams, 26, was arraigned on Oct. 28 on an indicted count of robbery in the first degree — taking property by force while armed with a deadly weapon — a Class A felony punishable by up to 20 years. An omnibus hearing is set for Dec. 10 and a trial week for Jan. 4, 2027. Case 4FA-26-01987CR.

Ryan Bud James, 46, was arraigned the same day on counts of first-degree vehicle theft, third-degree criminal mischief and third-degree assault. An omnibus hearing is set for Dec. 3 and a trial week for Dec. 21. Case 4FA-26-02067CR.

An arraignment set for Robbie Dale Bevard, 52, on Oct. 28 was vacated. He is charged on an indicted count of assault in the second degree — causing injury with a weapon with intent — a Class B felony punishable by up to 10 years, recorded as domestic violence. An omnibus hearing is set for Nov. 5 and a trial week for Nov. 23. Case 4FA-26-02068CR.
All three are charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Arraignment held in Anderson assault case: Gregory Steven Ashley
body: Gregory Steven Ashley, 47, is charged on two indicted counts of assault in the third degree — repeatedly threatening someone with death or injury — a Class C felony, punishable by up to five years. He also faces counts of second-degree terroristic threatening, driving under the influence, fourth-degree assault and driving with a canceled, suspended or revoked license. The offense is dated Oct. 9 at Anderson.
An arraignment and a bail hearing were held on Oct. 28. A calendar call is set for Nov. 17 and a trial week for Nov. 30. Case 4NE-26-00103CR. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Eleven Fairbanks case numbers opened with no defendant named remain without charges
body: Eleven criminal case numbers opened at the Fairbanks courthouse on Oct. 28, in which the court records the defendant only as “Grand Jury,” still carry no charging document, no charge, no hearing and no docket entry. Cases 4FA-26-02180CR through 4FA-26-02190CR.

None of the eleven appears in the court system's weekly charges report for Oct. 22 to 28, which was run on the evening of Oct. 28. A twelfth case number opened the same afternoon, which names a defendant, does appear in it.
